title: You’re not drowning because no one came.
paragraphs:
You’re not drowning because no one came.
You’re drowning… because you keep resisting the rescue.

Because this isn’t just a storm story.
This is you.
This is me.
This is every moment we chose control over surrender.
In Matthew 14, the scene is violent.

Wind tearing across the sea.
Waves crashing like judgment.
Night swallowing visibility.

And in the middle of it—
a man doing the impossible.

Because his eyes were locked on
Jesus Christ.

A glance sideways.
A shift in focus.
A whisper of fear.

Not instantly.
Not dramatically at first.

No performance.
No polished prayer.
Just desperation.
And the Bible says something that should wreck your pride:

“Immediately Jesus reached out His hand and caught him.”
(Matthew 14:31)

Not after Peter proved himself.
Not after he calmed down.
Not after he fixed his mess.
But here’s the tension you can’t ignore:

Peter had to stop trying to save himself
long enough
to be saved.

Because you’re fighting a battle
God never asked you to win alone.

You’re trying to outswim addiction.
Outrun guilt.
Outwork your shame.
Outthink your anxiety.
But His hand doesn’t just pull you up.

Out of control.
Out of denial.
Out of the identity you built to protect your wounds.

Because rescue feels like loss
before it feels like freedom.

Not every discomfort is the enemy.
Sometimes it’s the grip of grace.

When God confronts your sin—
that’s not rejection.
That’s rescue.

When He disrupts your plans—
that’s not punishment.
That’s protection.

When He calls you to surrender—
that’s not weakness.
The Gospel is not “fix yourself first.”

You were sinking in sin.
Helpless.
Powerless.
Unable to save yourself.
And Jesus Christ stepped into your storm.
He didn’t stand at a distance shouting instructions.

He took on flesh.
Walked into our chaos.
Lived without sin.
And then—

Not as a victim.
As a substitute.

For your rebellion.
For your pride.
For every moment you said,
“I don’t need You.”

Nails driven through it.
Blood poured out from it.
So that when it reaches for you—
it’s not just strong.

The hand that saves you
is the hand that conquered everything trying to drown you.
Why are you still fighting Him?

Why keep pushing away
the only One who can actually hold you?

Not tomorrow.
Not “when things calm down.”
Not “when you feel ready.”
Confess the sin you’ve been hiding.
Call on His name—not perfectly, just honestly:
He won’t shame you for sinking.
But you have to stop fighting.

You have to let go
to be lifted up.

Sit with it.
Send it to someone who’s drowning quietly.

Because someone you know is one surrender away
from a completely different story.

The only question is—
will you finally take His hand?
“We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.”
